tests.title: every input generates or refuses by design — no hard failures
tests.reason: ⚠️ THE ONE TO WATCH — 50.1% of the 30,000 ms budget and 39% of the whole suite's test time on its own. It generates thousands of plans across an exhaustive grid, which is the point: a sampled version could not make the claim in its title. It is the test that caused CI-TIMEOUT-01 (red on the old 5,000 ms default, at +1.4% on the day, having been over the line for weeks). ALLOWED, because exhaustiveness is doctrine here and the grid is the asset — but it has roughly one doubling of headroom left before the hard wall, and widening the grid again is a decision to make deliberately, not a diff to wave through.

tests.title: 🔴 no build-profile plan over its distance ceiling, 8–26 weeks out, any distance
tests.reason: INTENSITY-RUNWAY-01 (2026-10-19). The runway axis is the point: §1 broke at single runway lengths (100K 16/21 wk, HM 8–11, marathon 11) and no sweep varied runway one week at a time. ~1,330 plans (every runway 8–26 × every distance × strided envelope profiles). Cut from 27 s to ~5 s (stride 131 -> 401); falsified at this stride (the healthy yield off -> the engine throws on a 20.5% HM plan). Going wider again would trade the population for seconds; going narrower stops it reaching the yielded plans (5 at this stride).

tests.title: the CONSTRUCTED cohort is real, and the standing grids do not contain it
tests.reason: NOTE-LEVER-INJURY-CAP-01. Generates a cohort NEITHER standing grid contains: cohortGrid carries injury_history: [] and targetedGrid is Knee / Shin / Achilles, not back or plantar fasciitis, so the §9 Am. 3 long-run ceiling is unreachable without building the cell. The first arm pays for the whole corpus (lazily, so the cost lands in a test and not in import time) and the rest reuse it. Strided 23, not 7, which took it from 29.4s and 98.2% of budget to this with an identical verdict: 0 either way, and 0 un-strided over the full 41,472-row HM+ grid.

tests.title: NO quality session anywhere in the corpus is an aerobic row
tests.reason: QUALITY-AERO-FALLBACK-01, 2026-09-19. A CORPUS assertion: a quality slot must never be filled by an aerobic row. The traced single case is asserted separately and is fast; this one exists because the fallback is reachable from ANY thin pool, so one plan cannot make the claim in its title. Already SAMPLED with a coprime stride of 31 (a prefix would over-sample whichever axis the grid varies slowest — the bias the liveness work hit three times), which took it from 67s unsampled to 16.8s at stride 7 to 4.8s here. Going faster means sampling below ~500 quality sessions, at which point it can pass while the defect is live in a cohort it happened to miss.

tests.title: holds across the cohort and targeted grids
tests.reason: RULEENGINE-HIP-COMMENT-01, 2026-09-25. A CORPUS assertion of the same shape as qualityAeroFallback above, and cheaper: §4/§5's "base is all-easy" is the premise CB-HSR-AVOID-01 deleted a hip-flexor rule on, and a premise believed in a commit message is not a measured one. ALREADY SAMPLED DOWN ONCE: the full 45,776-plan grid measured 17,630 ms, so it walks a coprime stride over 1,200 inputs — a slice would be worse than slow, because a corpus walked from its head is the "debt was the SAMPLE, not the rules" failure this repo has recorded three times. It cannot shrink much further: the assertion carries a floor of 20 early-onset plans, and that cohort is 6.7% of the grid, so a much smaller sample would stop reaching the one mechanism that could actually break the premise.

tests.title: marathon: every refusal names a reachable next step
tests.reason: REFUSAL-COHERENCE-01, 2026-09-23. Generates the marathon refusal corpus and, for every refusal, re-runs generation at the base the refusal TOLD the runner to reach — the cost is a second full generation per refusal, and it is the whole point: the defect it was written for was a refusal naming a base the runner already had, which a single-pass check cannot see. ⚠️ IT SHIPPED UNBASELINED AND LEFT `npm run verify` EXITING 1 ON MAIN for the rest of the day, invisible because every test PASSED and the eye stops at the pass count. A non-zero exit behind a green test list is this repo's oldest shape.

tests.title: marathon: §44 — every refusal still names a next step
tests.reason: Same corpus as the case above, generated a second time for §44's separate obligation. Genuinely reducible by sharing one corpus across the file, which is the saving to take if this file ever needs one.

tests.title: the em-dash debt does not grow while BRAND-EMDASH-01 is open
tests.reason: Same corpus as the case above, generated a second time. Genuinely reducible — it is here as a baselined number rather than a fix because BRAND-EMDASH-01 closing removes the case entirely.

tests.title: no runner-facing string contains a section symbol (§)
tests.reason: Generates a plan corpus and walks every emitted string. The cost is the corpus, not the scan; sharing one corpus across this file's cases is the obvious saving if it ever needs one.

tests.title: 100K: refuses nobody today, so there is no refusal to be incoherent
tests.reason: 2026-09-25, INJURY-DELIVERED-COVERAGE-01. Re-baselined as CONTENTION, and the causal story I first wrote was WRONG and measured out. §94's delivered arm now runs for injury plans too, and `useCaseEnvelope` (this file's corpus) is ~50% injured, so 'validatePlan got twice as expensive here' was the obvious explanation for the 2.1x step. Measured standalone, twice each way: 8.25 s with the amendment, 8.05 s without — **~2%, not 2x.** The amendment is not the cause. What is: six test files were added to the suite today and these two are CPU-bound plan sweeps that lose more than linearly under worker contention (the gate itself reported a 1.34x run load against a 2.1x move). Recorded this way rather than as a confident attribution, because a baseline reason nobody can check is how a real regression gets waved through later.

tests.title: 🔴 THE DEFECT, REPRODUCED: with NO plan_start, Sunday and Monday generate different plans
tests.reason: COHORT-REVIEW-CLOCK-01. Generates the marathon envelope TWICE under two faked system clocks (Sunday and Monday), because that divergence IS the defect and nothing cheaper reproduces it — `todayOverride` cannot, which is why two earlier versions of this gate were vacuous. Thinned from every 25th case to every 60th (8,282 ms -> 2,898 ms); thinning further would start to threaten the vacuity arm, which asserts the sample is non-empty. 9.7% of budget.

tests.title: passes its own falsification suite in both directions
tests.reason: Spawns git roughly thirty times: it builds a throwaway repository in a temp dir and makes a real commit per case. The cost IS the test. ⚠️ It used to be near-instant, because it pinned SHAs from this repo's own history — and that version FAILED IN CI, where actions/checkout@v4 defaults to fetch-depth 1 and none of those commits exist. Worse than the three red cases: FOUR of its six "passes" were hollow, reading ok only because the base ref was unreachable so the filter fell through to BUILD, which was what they expected anyway. A synthetic repo cannot be shallow, cannot age out, and cannot be rewritten under the test. Paying 2.7s for that is the right trade. If it ever needs to be cheaper, the git calls can be batched with a single fast-import rather than dropping cases.

tests.title: the offer only appears when switching the goal ACTUALLY generates a plan
tests.reason: Generates a plan per candidate goal to prove the offer is never made against a goal that would itself refuse. The second generation IS the assertion — an offer checked against anything cheaper is the claim/computation mismatch class.

tests.title: 🔴 the 10K race simulation repeats for every runner, inside 60% of the race
tests.reason: Baselined 2026-11-03 and NOT caused by the change it surfaced on. The file was last touched by 8ff976b7 (MP-BLOCKS-ONE-BLOCK-01 / TENK-SIM-ONE-REP-01) and contains ZERO references to strides, neuromuscular or hills, so §28 Am.4 cannot reach it — checked rather than assumed. It crossed the 1500 ms reporting line at **1517 ms normalised (17 ms, 1.1%)** under a 2.72x loaded run, which several neighbours in the same report call 'too close to the line to call'. The cost is inherent to its claim: 'for EVERY runner' means a corpus, and a sampled version could not make the assertion in its title — the same argument as targetedGrid.test.ts above. ⚠️ Declared rather than silently absorbed: if it climbs materially above this figure the cause is a real slowdown, not load, and it should be investigated then.

tests.title: generated notes read in hours past the hour, and still exist
tests.reason: Generates a large plan corpus; the cost is the coverage.

tests.title: NO session in the corpus claims race pace unless it is stamped race_pace
tests.reason: PEAK-NOTE-PACE-CLAIM-01. A CORPUS assertion, and the cost IS the coverage: it walks every session of every generated plan asking whether a note claims race pace on a session that is not at race pace. A traced single case cannot answer that — the defect it guards was a claim that was true for the plans someone looked at and false elsewhere. First baselined 2026-11-08 at 1,592 ms (1.12% of the suite) when the 6-worker pool re-measurement moved every entry; it was over the reporting line before that and simply never crossed it on a measured run.

tests.title: ✅ THE FIX: passing the envelope's own plan_start makes the two days identical
tests.reason: COHORT-REVIEW-CLOCK-01, the other half. Same double generation under two faked clocks, proving the pinned plan_start removes the dependence. Cheaper than its sibling only because fewer cases refuse. 5.1% of budget.

tests.title: no runner-facing copy names toning
tests.reason: Walks every runner-facing and marketing source file from disk rather than a listed set, because a claim-absence check is only as wide as its population and a hand-maintained list is the hole. The cost is the tree walk, not generation.

tests.title: on REAL plans, the annotated week is always easier than both neighbours
tests.reason: GATE-FALSIFY-01 (a) shape 3, 2026-09-24. Measured 1.6–1.7s STANDALONE, i.e. genuinely over the 1500 ms line and not an artefact of what else was running: it generates real plans and checks the annotated week against BOTH neighbours, which is the claim in its title and cannot be made from a fixture. ⚠️ SURFACED BY ADDING AN UNRELATED TEST FILE — the two were sitting just under the line and one more file's scheduling tipped them over, which means they would have tripped on a loaded CI runner anyway. Baselined rather than ignored, and deliberately NOT made faster by sampling: a sampled version would pass while the defect is live in the weeks it skipped.

tests.title: on REAL plans, the annotated week is NEVER the peak (Wood, binding)
tests.reason: Asserts the marketing reveal against REAL generated plans from cohortGrid rather than a fixture, because the claim is about what the engine actually produces; a fixture would let the page and the engine drift apart, which is the defect class this file exists for.

tests.title: 2. ACROSS THE COHORT: no non-returning runner sees "coming back"
tests.reason: Generates across the cohort to prove no NON-returning runner ever sees the "coming back" cause. A negative claim over a population cannot be made on one plan, and this is the arm that would catch the cause leaking to the wrong runner.

tests.title: and the invariant agrees — producer and checker, not one of them
tests.reason: Runs three corpora (cohortGrid, targetedGrid, slowGoalGrid) because the producer and the invariant must be shown to agree on the DELIVERED week, not the internal curve: ADR-022 class. One corpus would leave the other two cohorts unchecked, and a checker sharing the producer one grid is the shape DELOAD-OWNER-01 names.

tests.title: Today's card carries it on an eased day
tests.reason: Globs and renders the real component tree rather than asserting on source text, because a source assertion passes on a comment. The cost is the render, and the alternative is a hollow check.

tests.title: 3. the residual is NOT suppressed — large leaps still exist and are still counted
tests.reason: Generates the use-case envelope to show the residual is NOT suppressed: large week-1 leaps still exist and are still said. Proving a warning survives needs the population that triggers it, which a fixture cannot supply.

tests.title: no plan is told it missed the floor by less than one rounding step
tests.reason: Generates plans to prove no runner is told they missed the §24 floor by less than one rounding step, and that the two enforcement sites agree on what the floor IS. Both are claims about every plan, so the corpus is the test.

tests.title: 🔴 INV-PLAN-REPEATS-REPEAT is silent on every served plan
tests.reason: INV-PLAN-REPEATS-REPEAT's liveness arm. A CORPUS assertion by necessity: it generates across the cohort to show the invariant is SILENT on every served plan, which is the only way to tell a working rule from a dead one — a single traced case proves neither. First baselined 2026-11-08 at 1,005 ms (0.72% of the suite); it sits just over the 1,000 ms reporting line and crosses it with ordinary noise, so expect it to come and go from this register rather than drift.

tests.title: the two §24 enforcement sites agree on what the floor is
tests.reason: Generates plans to prove no runner is told they missed the §24 floor by less than one rounding step, and that the two enforcement sites agree on what the floor IS. Both are claims about every plan, so the corpus is the test.

tests.title: the population is real — an empty one would pass every arm below vacuously
tests.reason: ⚠️ CORPUS ARM, AND IT WAS SLOW BEFORE TODAY — `check:slow` could not see it because it was reading a two-day-stale report (`CHECK-SLOW-STALE-01` was fixed the same day this test landed, and the eight tests that had crossed the 1,000 ms line in those two days were exactly this class). It generates real plans to prove §52's lopsided-week residual is maintenance-only, which is the claim its own title makes about the POPULATION: an empty or synthetic corpus would pass every arm in the file vacuously, which is the failure shape this repo keeps paying for. The corpus is lazy and memoised across arms and already re-strided 7 → 23 to cut it from 29.4 s to the current figure. ALLOWED: the cost buys a real population, and a sampled version could not make the claim.

tests.title: planRationaleNotes returns the same notes, in the same order, in both units
tests.reason: ⚠️ INCIDENTAL DRIFT, NOT CAUSED BY THE SHIP THAT RECORDED IT. Flagged NEW on 2026-11-13 by GRID-NO-MENOPAUSAL-TENDON-01's run, and that ship cannot have caused it: this test reads `cohortGrid`, which was untouched (41,472 rows, asserted by `cohortGridSize.test.ts` on the same run); the six new rows went into `targetedGridExtra`, which this file never imports. So it is one of the tests CHECK-SLOW-STALE-01 describes — crossing the 1,000 ms reporting line between report reads, unflagged until somebody ran the gate against a fresh report. 1,469 ms raw / 1,534 ms normalised at this run's 0.96x load, 4.9% of the 30,000 ms budget. ALLOWED: it generates plans across the grid in BOTH unit systems to prove the note set is identical, and a sampled version could not make that claim — the same reasoning the `targetedGrid.test.ts` entry carries. ⚠️ Recorded rather than optimised, and recorded as somebody else's drift so the next reader does not attribute it to the grid change in the same commit.
